RIPLEY, W.Va. (WV News) - Ripley suffered a couple of shutouts on the pitch in girls' soccer recently, earned a win and was involved in not one, but two ties.
Nitro handed Ripley a 9-0 defeat.
"They have everyone back from a very good team last year and their place is always a hard place to play," said head coach Jay Pierson. "The girls battled the whole game and fought hard and hopefully learned from the defeat."
Shelby Keefer had 14 saves for the Lady Vikings.
Sissonville secured a 5-0 win over Ripley.
"We came out flat and struggled to find any rhythm in the first half and got down, 4-0. We made some adjustments and got more focused and only gave up one goal in the second half."
Keefer had six saves and Lexi Donohew had five.
Ripley came away with a 1-0 win over Scott. Audrey Scholl had the goal with Bella Lee being credited with the assist.
"It was a hard-played game by both sides. We played short-handed, having two girls who didn't make the trip due to illness, leaving us with only one sub after an injury. I'm proud of the girls for giving their all and staying focused and patient to secure a win."
Following the victory, Ripley battled to a pair of 0-0 ties with Williamstown and Lincoln County.
Keefer had six saves against Williamstown and five in the showdown with Lincoln County.
